text.p: Flamboyant former Colombian international goalkeeper Rene Higuita was suspended by his club Atletico Nacional on Wednesday after repeatedly missing training and failing to justify his absences.

Higuita, who has entertained fans worldwide with his eccentric and apparently carefree attitude to goalkeeping, had rejoined the Medellin club only three months ago after previously quitting in November.
Last year he also opted out of the national team, claiming he was not fit enough for international soccer.
Since then, Higuita, 30, has seen himself outdone in the eccentricity stakes by rivals such as Paraguay's Jose Luis Chilavert, who has become a regular scorer of free-kicks and penalties.
Club sources said former South American champions Atletico would try to sell Higuita to an overseas team and were talking with clubs in Argentina, Brazil and the United States.
Higuita, who played in the 1990 World Cup, missed the 1994 tournament after being held in prison for six months on charges, later dropped, of breaking Colombia's anti-kidnapping laws.
He subsequently made an international comeback but dropped out again shortly after making an astonishing "scorpion" save with his feet against England in a friendly international.
Last December, Higuita's home in Medellin, Colombia's second city, was bombed by unidentified attackers.
Police said the intruders forced their way past a maid and detonated dynamite, which damaged windows, doors and furniture but caused no injuries.
